links.comparator_used: Alerts sent directly to physicians without pharmacist review (compared within the same CDSS, retrospective, non-randomized)
links.outcome: Physician acceptance rate and physician alert burden
links.effect: Of 10,556 alerts, 619 went directly to physicians (acceptance 89.8%) and 2,231 reached physicians after pharmacist evaluation (acceptance 68.4%); overall acceptance 72.4%. All hospital physicians together received 7.8 notifications per day.
links.tradeoff: Clinical pharmacists received 17.2 alerts per day to review. Acceptance was lower for pharmacist-reviewed alerts than for direct alerts, and the two groups were not randomized.
links.quote: Involving clinical pharmacists proved a promising approach to limit the alert burden of physicians and thus tackle alert fatigue.

design_hint: pharmacist review of alerts before physician notification
